title: Browsing a Neighborhood Record Shop
description: Sort through album bins, sleeves, and artist names in a small record shop.
cardDescription: Sort through album bins, sleeves, and artist names in a small record shop.
focus: The clues distinguish a recording's packaging from its label and the store's sorting system.
solvingTip: Try the shop fixtures before the music-format words.

answerNotes.SLEEVE: A sleeve protects the disc; an inner sleeve may sit inside an outer jacket.
answerNotes.BIN: Record bins allow customers to browse sleeves upright.
answerNotes.GENRE: Genre describes a style category rather than the artist's name.
answerNotes.USED: Used identifies ownership history, not necessarily the disc's condition.
answerNotes.LABEL: Label can mean the printed center or the issuing company.

title: Reading an Album Cover
description: Discover the artist credits, liner notes, and printed details surrounding a favorite album.
cardDescription: Discover the artist credits, liner notes, and printed details surrounding a favorite album.
focus: An album cover identifies the release, while liner notes can supply background and performer credits.
solvingTip: Use the clue to tell a person's role from a printed section.

Printed acknowledgment naming a contributor to an album

answerNotes.LINER: Liner notes can describe the music, performers, and circumstances of recording.
answerNotes.CREDIT: Credits identify roles such as musician, writer, or producer.
answerNotes.PORTRAIT: A portrait is one possible cover design, not a requirement for an album.
answerNotes.TITLE: An album title can differ from the title of any individual song.
answerNotes.PRODUCER: A producer's responsibilities vary between recordings and working arrangements.

answerNotes.CASSETTE: A cassette holds supply and take-up reels inside a protective shell.
answerNotes.REWIND: Rewinding moves tape backward without normal listening playback.
answerNotes.SPOOL: Two reels exchange tape as the cassette plays.
answerNotes.HEAD: The tape head interacts with the magnetic pattern carried on the tape.
answerNotes.EJECT: Eject opens or releases the cassette rather than erasing its sound.

title: Listening Through Stereo Headphones
description: Match the left and right channels, ear cushions, and volume control of a personal listening session.
cardDescription: Match the left and right channels, ear cushions, and volume control of a personal listening session.
focus: Stereo uses separate channels; a mono recording does not become stereo merely by using two earcups.

answerNotes.HEADPHONES: Headphones let one listener hear sound close to each ear.
answerNotes.STEREO: The channels can carry different information that creates a spatial impression.
answerNotes.CHANNEL: A channel is a signal path rather than a genre of music.
answerNotes.MONO: A mono signal may be played through both earcups without becoming stereo.
answerNotes.CUSHION: The cushion contacts the listener's head around the ear.

answerNotes.REEL: Open-reel machines expose the reels rather than enclosing them in a cassette.
answerNotes.SPLICE: A tape splice can edit a recording by joining selected portions.
answerNotes.LEADER: Leader helps thread and protect the recorded portion.
answerNotes.CAPSTAN: The capstan works with a pressure roller to move tape steadily.
answerNotes.TAKEUP: The take-up reel gathers tape after it passes through the playback path.
